precepts.text: From the sit down: unto us a child is born. Who's the us? When you read up in the chapter, it's talking about the nation of Israel. His name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father: Christ holds the title of God, but do not confuse that with his father. Christ is called the everlasting father because he created us. God the Father begat Christ, and Christ created us. He was giving it to them plain and simple, taking his time, and they still couldn't get it.
precepts.point: Theology is a dangerous drug. These cemetery schools are dangerous for our community. White supremacy taught them the Bible; they get a certificate from going to school and learning their curriculum. We get a reward for doing God's law, statutes, and commandments: an everlasting reward with the father.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
At the sit-down with the men from theology school, this was read to them: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”. Who is the us? Read up in the chapter and it is talking about the nation of Israel. “and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

Christ holds the title of God, but do not confuse that with his Father. Christ is called the everlasting Father because he created us. God the Father begat Christ, which is the creation of God, and Christ created us. It was read to them plain and simple, taking time, and you could hear it: Christ is called the mighty God and the everlasting Father. They still could not get it. They said creation does not mean creation, it means something else.

That is what Paul feared: “as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.” The serpent was a real slick one. He tricked Eve, like he is tricking the people in these Christian churches, when the scriptures are so plain to be understood.

It is a simple thing that Christ had an earthly father named Joseph, through Joseph's seed. It is a simple thing that Christ is not the same person as his Father. Many scriptures were gone through showing that the Father and the Son are two different people, and the confusion comes from the Christian churches.

precepts.text: Unto us a child is born: possessive again. His name shall be called the Prince of Peace. Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end: when it is time for Christ to return and the Israelites to reign, there is no end to it. The Lord sent his word into Jacob, and it lighted upon Israel. So our peace is talking about Israel's peace.
precepts.point: But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. Who was afar off? Israel. These Ephesians in Ephesus are Israelites scattered in Ephesus. He is our peace: not everybody's peace. Christ is the peace that brings both nations, the southern and northern kingdom, back together.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Ephesians says “he is our peace”, so go to the prophecy of the Prince of Peace. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, possessive again. “and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” When it's time for Christ to return and the Israelites to reign, there is not going to be any end to it. “The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

Then: “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.” So our peace is Israel's peace. Christ is the peace that brings both nations, the southern and the northern kingdom, back together. That is the both he made one.

precepts.text: This is a prophecy written by Isaiah: he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali. Assyrian captivity, wham. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light. Isaiah is prophesying and Matthew is revealing what it's really talking about.
precepts.point: From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. So Christ was that great light that was being spoken of.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Some Israelites had come back to the land, and watch what they were calling part of the kingdom of Israel: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” They were calling them Gentiles.

Isaiah wrote it first as prophecy: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” That affliction is the Assyrian captivity: wham. Zebulun and Naphtali were carried away, and their land became Galilee of the nations, of the Gentiles.

Then Isaiah says what would come to them: “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” Matthew gives it back as “The people which sat in darkness saw great light.” Isaiah is prophesying and Matthew is revealing what it is really talking about.

“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ was that great light spoken of, shining on the scattered tribes of Israel that had been made Gentiles.

precepts.text: Philip said, Lord, shew us the Father. Christ answered, have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? He that hath seen me hath seen the Father. What is he telling Philip? I created you; I am your everlasting Father; you were brought forth through me.
precepts.point: Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end. It behooves us to learn God's laws, commandments, and statutes, because to set up a government you need everything we read at the beginning of class about what a community consists of. God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

precepts.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made by him, and without him was not any thing made that was made. The Father alone begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created. That is why he said to Philip, have I been so long with you and you have not known me? We have to shake the Christian thoughts, the Baptist and Catholic residue in the head.

In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs. That is the increase of his government. We are still at the mustard seed stage right now; this is small, and it is going to grow. And remember what was added in class: everything you lay your eyes on came from a thought first. When we understand the power God gave us in the mind and remove the doubt and the fear, untapped greatness is waiting to bud.

God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

precepts.text: Solomon learned wisdom diligently and communicated her liberally; they that use her become the friends of God. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today: God gave him certain knowledge of the things that are, to know how the world was made and the operation of the elements, the beginning, ending, and midst of the times, the alterations of the turning of the sun, the change of seasons, the circuits of years, the positions of stars, the natures of living creatures, the furies of wild beasts, the violence of winds, the reasonings of men, the diversities of plants, and the virtues of roots. We are not on Solomon's level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, but that is what the mustard seed government is going to grow into.

God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

precepts.text: I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations do not want that; some of us may not even want that. It is coming anyway. In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.
precepts.point: Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end. It behooves us to learn God's laws, commandments, and statutes, because to set up a government you need everything we read at the beginning of class about what a community consists of. God's laws are going to filter everything for us. And we have to learn to think bigger: not a house, not property; the world is ours. In order for the world to be ours, we have to be able to set up all of those things.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want that either: I don’t want no justice and judgment, hell no. Yes, it is coming anyway.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

precepts.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder. A lot of people do not understand why Christ is called the everlasting Father: because the one you think is the heavenly Father in the Old Testament was actually Christ. Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice. That is law and order. Some do not like law and order because they like chaos; the Bible can break that spirit, but only if you let it. This is the beginning of God's government: that is why we establish law, order, and rank, and teach the laws, commandments, and statutes of the Holy Bible.
precepts.point: And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness. The throne that is going to be established is the throne of Christ.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David.” The throne that is going to be established is the throne of Christ, and Isaiah 9 shows it: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” The government shall be upon the shoulders of Christ.

“and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” A lot of people don’t understand why he is called the everlasting Father. It is because the one you think is the heavenly Father in the Old Testament was actually Christ. That is why there is a lot of confusion in the Israelite community.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Don’t just read by that word increase; the mustard seed of Matthew 13 shows it. We are at the mustard seed stage now, and this is the beginning of God’s government.

“upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” To order it and establish it with judgment and justice: that is law and order. That is why we establish law, order and rank, and teach brothers and sisters the laws, commandments and statutes of the Holy Bible.

Some don’t like law because they like adultery better; they don’t like order because they like disorder, chaos, a toxic marriage and a chaotic life, married today and divorced tomorrow. That is genetic encoding from slavery, and it is in all of us. But the Bible can break that spirit, only if you let it. Only God can cleanse that from you, and his throne, established in mercy, is judging and “hasting righteousness.”

precepts.text: Galilee of the nations: so the nations also means the Gentiles. What we read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament. When the prophets spoke, they substantiated their points from this text.
precepts.point: The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Matthew writes “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”, and Isaiah had already written it: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

Matthew says “Galilee of the Gentiles”; Isaiah says “Galilee of the nations.” So the nations also means the Gentiles. Same land, same people, same word.

What we read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament. When the apostles and prophets spoke, they had to substantiate their points from what we call the Old Testament today. Whatever they said, they had to be able to justify it with that text. Matthew is not saying something new; he is showing the prophecy fulfilled.

This is the foundation for Acts 10. By the biblical text the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles, like strangers, like heathens. The New Testament shows Paul going out to find them scattered among the nations and bring them back to God, because the prophecy sent from the Old Testament was that the job was to raise up the 12 tribes of Israel again. The Gentiles of Galilee are Israelites that were scattered and cut off, and God is gathering them back.

precepts.text: Every battle of the warrior is with confused noise and garments rolled in blood, but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.
precepts.point: The people shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut up burnt in the fire. Not the fire of 2 Kings: Isaiah 9:5, every battle of the warrior is with confused noise and garments rolled in blood, but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire, thermonuclear fire.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Isaiah 33 ends: “And the people shall be as the burnings of lime: as thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.” There is going to be fire, but it is not the kind of fire we read about in 2 Kings, men being burnt up with fire from heaven in that way. Isaiah 9 shows what kind of fire it is.

“For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood.” That is how battles have always been fought: noise, confusion, men's garments rolled in blood.

“But this shall be with burning and fuel of fire.” This battle is going to be with fire. What kind of fire? Thermonuclear fire.

That is the fire of Isaiah 33, where Lebanon is ashamed and hewn down, Sharon, which is Tel Aviv, is like a wilderness, Bashan, which is Syria, and Carmel in northern Israel shake off their fruits. The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceases, and the valiant ones, the generals and armies, cry without. The people are burned like lime and like thorns cut up, and then the Lord says, “Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.”

precepts.text: The leaders of this people cause them to err, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord shall have no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer and every mouth speaketh folly.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
“The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites.” Zion is another name for Israel, and fearfulness will surprise the hypocrites of our people. Isaiah 9 gives the example.

“For the leaders of this people cause them to err.” These are the religious leaders and the political leaders of our people. Our leaders in this society cause us to err, cause us to sin, because we follow what they say and it is always against God. “And they that are led of them are destroyed.” You followed T.D. Jakes? You followed Pastor P and the other dudes on the screen? Destroyed.

“Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men.” Because they follow foolish religious leaders and foolish political leaders. “Neither shall have mercy on their fatherless and widows”: God is not going to have mercy on the fatherless children and the widows whose husbands died.

“For every one is an hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaketh folly.” Every one of them is a hypocrite. They all have the Bible, they say they believe in Jesus, but they won't do nary a word in that book. Every mouth speaks lies; as soon as they open their black lips, it's a lie, and it isn't in the scriptures. “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.”

Look at the churches: holy water and holy kisses, people falling out saying they have the Holy Spirit. That is why the racist white man says all the Black churches need to be shut down and come learn from the white man how to serve God. And now there are Israelites who know they are Israel speaking in tongues and calling it a heavenly language, bringing the lies of foolishness into this truth. Those are the hypocrites the fear will surprise.

precepts.text: Unto us a child is born, and the government shall be upon his shoulder; the church of Acts 7 is the government of Christ. He is called the everlasting Father because much of the Old Testament's Father is Christ; have I been so long time with you, Philip, and hast thou not known me? Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end: it starts as a mustard seed and grows, and once started there is no stopping it.
precepts.point: Be preemptive with the Christians who run to Exodus 12:38, the mixed multitude, to say other nations were part of the church. Leviticus 25:45-46: of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you shall ye buy, and they shall be your bondmen for ever. The mixed multitude were our slaves.

note.label: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.why:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” When Acts 7:38 speaks of “the church in the wilderness”, it is speaking of the government of Christ. That church was Israel, the twelve tribes, and it is his government that rests upon his shoulder.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” Christ is called the everlasting Father because many times in the Old Testament, when you read about the Father, it is making reference to Christ. That is why, when Philip asked Christ to show them the Father, Christ answered that he had been so long time with him and still Philip had not known him. Christ is letting you know: I am the father that created you. Not the Father, but your father.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Increase means it starts small. Christ said the kingdom of heaven starts like a mustard seed, but in the end it is the largest. Once that mustard seed is planted and growing, there is no stopping it. It sits “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

This truth cannot be stopped. No matter how many Israelites they attempt to kill or arrest, the church that was in the wilderness, the government on Christ’s shoulder, keeps increasing and has no end.

precepts.text: Israel hath cast off the thing that is good, the law, and the enemy shall pursue him. They have set up kings, but not by me; of their silver and gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off. You make these pastors your idols and work to get them their thousand dollars.
precepts.point: The pastors are the new taskmasters, sent out by Esau with his doctrines, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold to give him your last.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” Who are the leaders in the Black community today? Your Black leaders have you fighting for Palestinians and fighting all kinds of stupid battles. And you Black Christians that are led of them are destroyed. Our people are so destroyed they don't even know it: destroyed with a warm fuzzy feeling every Sunday. The pastors are the new taskmasters. They get sent out by Esau, they learned the doctrines from Esau, and they bring it into your community, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold and give him your last.

Hosea shows how it came to this. “Israel hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him.” What is good? The laws of God, this Bible. Israel cast them off, and because of that the enemy pursues him.

“They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not.” You set up leaders, brothers and sisters, but it isn't of the Lord. “Of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” You make these men, these so-called leaders, your idols. You follow them wholeheartedly. Pastor says he needs an extra thousand dollars and you say, Pastor, I'mma work it out, I'mma get you your money. That's cold pimping.

And look at the fruit: a grandmother in Jamal Bryant's church sowing her twelve hundred dollars and being embarrassed because it was not enough; Eddie Long on the throne while the white man holds the mic and tells him he is no longer a commoner. These are your leaders that cause you to err.

“That they may be cut off.” And now we are cut off. That is what comes of casting off the law of God and setting up kings the Lord never chose.

precepts.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways. Yet tomorrow morning our people will be in church drinking the doctrine of the men who enslaved them.
precepts.point: The pastors are the new taskmasters, sent out by Esau with his doctrines, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold to give him your last.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Put the oppressors on the screen: Pope Nicholas V and Pope Alexander VI. In 1452 Pope Nicholas V issued Dum Diversas, authorizing King Alfonso V of Portugal to fight, subjugate and conquer the Saracens and pagans in African territory. Those were good Christians.

Think about it. Without those two devils, those two Christians, there would be no such thing as an African-American, a Jamaican, a Haitian, a Puerto Rican. We are named after whatever landmass we were scattered to, and we are the result of those men. Christians did this to us. And now we revel in it, reverence them, and follow their laws and their ways of life.

The scripture says choose none of his ways. But tomorrow at 11 o'clock Sunday morning, where will all our people be? Not listening to the truth. They will be in church getting a good dose of the doctrine of the man that enslaved them, that turned them into African-Americans and Jamaicans and Haitians. They can't wait to go learn about a good Jesus.

That is the leaders of Isaiah 9:16 causing our people to err. Look at the results of being taught Christianity: a man on television saying he is a Christian first and that black is a construct, when the white man put us in chains and did not do that to his own people; a girl who let a boy call her the N-word and call him master; our people turning up on each other and showing teeth to everybody else. That is what comes of envying the oppressor and choosing his ways.

precepts.text: What shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? What do the celebrities give in exchange for their souls? Their bodies, to Amalek.
precepts.point: The pastors are the new taskmasters, sent out by Esau with his doctrines, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold to give him your last.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Terence Crawford said there was not a number that could get him back in that ring, and then said for 100 million dollars you can have my soul. That nigger was dead serious; look at his eyes. That is a dangerous man: a man who would sell out his mama and his children and do anything for money. That is the result of 400 years with Esau, and he just said out loud what the majority of Black celebrities, rappers and singers think.

“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” Esau gives you whatever you want: all the riches, all the connections, all the power, wealth you can't run from. But in order to get it, you lose your own soul.

“Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?” What do these celebrities give in exchange for their souls? Their booty. They give it up, and Amalek takes it. Your Jay-Zs and 50 Cents, your Mariah Careys and Whitneys: they have to give in order to receive.

What are you going to stand for if everything is about money? You have no dignity and no morals. These are the results of the leaders of this people causing them to err, and of Black Christians led by them being destroyed. There are no laws with them, because they were taught the laws are done away with.

precepts.text: Under Josiah, money for the temple came from Manasseh, Ephraim and all the remnant of Israel.
precepts.point: The Lord sent a word into Jacob and it lighted on Israel, and all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Under Josiah, when the money for the house of God was brought to Hilkiah the high priest, it was “the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites that kept the doors had gathered of the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, and of all the remnant of Israel, and of all Judah and Benjamin”.

Manasseh donated toward the temple in Jerusalem, and Ephraim donated too. Why “the remnant of Israel”? Because Assyria had taken most of them out of the land in waves; remnants remained, some idolatrous and some faithful. And that was during Josiah’s reign: whenever Judah is on point, Ephraim follows along.

Then Isaiah speaks to those same northern lands: “the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali”, afflicted “by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” Zebulun came to keep the Passover in Hezekiah’s day, and Tobit was of Naphtali. Galilee of the Gentiles is where the northern kingdom resided, and they were called Gentiles. “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light”: the people of verse 1, the northern kingdom.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, not all. He is the Prince of Peace because he must bring peace between those who have hatred for each other, so that there is no more division between the two kingdoms. “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel. And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria”. The same Ephraim and Manasseh whose remnant gave to the house of God in Judah’s good days would see the light of the son born of Judah.

precepts.text: Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.
precepts.point: A king shall reign in righteousness and princes rule in judgment.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
The saints will “possess the kingdom for ever, even for ever and ever.” Whose kingdom is it? Isaiah says: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” That is Christ. His name is called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

Read on: “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” It is Christ's government, and there shall be no end to it. That is why the saints take the kingdom for ever.

It is “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.” Christ orders the kingdom and establishes it with judgment and justice, and the saints possess it with him.

That is the answer to the city that became an harlot. Isaiah says it was once “full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.” There was a time we were righteous; now we kill each other like it is nothing, and every one loveth gifts. But the Lord will purge away our dross and restore us, and under Christ's government the saints will rule for ever.

precepts.text: His name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor.
precepts.point: Christ is the Counsellor, and his counsel is not found on the world's couch.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” He was so lustful and covetous for the petty things this world provides that he loses his soul: he does not get the kingdom. You had a million gazillion dollars and still could not pay your way into heaven. Then Christ says, “Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words”, and Isaiah shows who those words belong to.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor.” That child is Christ, and these are his titles. Stop right there: Counsellor. Christ is the ultimate counselor. The counsel for everything you are dealing with in this world, in this captivity, is already here in his words.

But you despise Christ's words, brothers and sisters. You don't even want to pick up your Bible and read four chapters, or pick up the precept packet to learn how to move this weapon. You are ashamed that Christ, the ultimate physician, has the fix for you. You can't get this counsel on a damn white man's couch. You can't go to Dr. Phil and expect him to fix your life. Them demons can't fix your life; they destroy homes. And Christ's counsel is free. How is it black people love free stuff, but when Christ gives it to you for free, you deny it?

Some purposely avoid the counselors in the truth because they have itching ears, and go to those as new as themselves, because they don't want to hear: fix your house, stop watching porn, delete the apps, get a flip phone, stop hanging with the same folks. Whoever is ashamed of the Counsellor's words, the laws, statutes and commandments, the blueprint to get out of this demonic land, Christ will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father.

precepts.text: Unto us a child is born, and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
precepts.point: Paul confirms it: all our fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, and they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. The Corinthians Paul wrote were Israelites, for Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses' day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and the seventy elders “saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.” Sapphire is blue, and the blue flame is the hottest part of a flame. Upon the nobles he laid not his hand: “also they saw God, and did eat and drink.”

Since no man hath seen God at any time, the one they saw and ate before was Christ. Isaiah calls him God: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” The child born to us is called the mighty God and the everlasting Father. That is the God of Israel the elders saw.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

precepts.text: This is the prophecy of Galilee of the Gentiles, the land of Zebulun and Naphtali by the sea.
precepts.point: The dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, and afterward more grievously afflicted her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.

note.label: Isaiah 9: For Unto Us a Child Is Born

precepts.why:
Isaiah speaks of “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” Matthew reads it back: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”.

This is the prophecy of Galilee of the Gentiles, the land of Zebulun and Naphtali by the sea, beyond Jordan. Galilee of the nations in Isaiah is Galilee of the Gentiles in Matthew, the same land of the two tribes.

precepts.text: The Most High returns to his place until, in their affliction, the people seek him early.
precepts.point: The people turn not to him that smites them, neither do they seek the Lord of hosts.

note.label: Isaiah 9: For Unto Us a Child Is Born

precepts.why:
The people would not turn to him that smote them, and would not seek the Lord of hosts. Hosea shows what the Most High does with a people like that: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face”. He withdraws and leaves them to their affliction.

But the affliction has a purpose: “in their affliction they will seek me early.” The smiting in Isaiah 9:13 is meant to turn the people back to him, and when they will not turn, he returns to his place until the affliction makes them acknowledge their offence and seek his face.

precepts.text: The prophecy quoted, naming the same land and the same people that saw great light.
precepts.point: The scripture calls that country Galilee of the Gentiles. Zebulun and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and this is the key to who the gentiles are that the gospel goes to after the southern kingdom rejects it.

note.label: Matthew 4: The Temptation in the Wilderness and the Calling of the Fishers

precepts.why:
When John was cast into prison, Christ departed into Galilee and dwelt in Capernaum, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim, “That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet”. Isaiah names the same land and the same people: “the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali”, afflicted “by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.”

Zebulun and Naphtali are tribes of the northern kingdom, and the scripture calls that country Galilee of the Gentiles, Galilee of the nations. The people that sat in darkness and saw great light were those tribes.

This is the key to who the gentiles are that the gospel goes to after the southern kingdom rejects it. The Gentiles of Galilee are Israelites of the northern tribes, the very people Isaiah said the light would shine on, and Christ dwelt among them so that it would be fulfilled.

precepts.text: The land of Zebulun and Naphtali, the people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

“The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” The land of Zebulun and Naphtali, the northern tribes driven into darkness, are the ones who saw the great light. That light is Christ, and Matthew says so plainly.

precepts.text: Manasseh and Ephraim are named together, confirming the darkened people are the northern tribes.
precepts.point: "Galilee of the Gentiles" proves the point, because those northern tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, broken and driven into darkness, are the people who saw the great light when Christ came preaching, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." They sat in the shadow of death because Ephraim was broken and taken into Assyria.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: and they together shall be against Judah.”

Manasseh and Ephraim are named together, and that confirms who the darkened people are: the northern tribes. The people of Galilee of the Gentiles who walked in darkness are Israel's north, set against Judah, and they are the Gentiles Peter speaks of.

precepts.point: When it says 'according to the will of God and our Father,' God refers to Christ (who is called God in Hebrews 1:8) and Father refers to the Most High.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

The son who is given is Christ, and his name is called The mighty God. That is why “God” in “according to the will of God and our Father” refers to Christ; he is God, and the Father is the Most High. The child born unto us is the one who gave himself for our sins.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: “And the government shall be upon his shoulder”: God is setting up a government under Christ, with the twelve, and under them the rest of the 144,000. “And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace”: one of his names is the everlasting Father. When you thought you were dealing with the Father throughout the scriptures, most of it is Christ.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“For the leaders of this people cause them to err”. Black people look at Nicki Minaj, a rapper, as a leader and spokesperson. Our daughters follow her telling them it's okay to be a hoe. We want marriage counsel from Steve Harvey when he's in his third marriage. Bad leadership. “and they that are led of them are destroyed.” Look at us: destroyed as a people because we follow everything except what God said. We follow what makes us feel good.

The Bible isn't a feel-good book. If you're looking to feel good, you're in the wrong place. It's the book that tells a black man and woman how evil they are and how to get their minds right. Christians don't believe it: you're not under the law, you're under grace; wear pants, God won't do anything. Everybody does whatever the hell they want, just like Judges 21:25. Turn sisters into hoes and single mothers and say God will forgive you. That's not in the Bible.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
Christ says another name: our God is the Almighty. People keep on playing with the Bible. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God,” You see that part, The mighty God? That is why he said he was called the Almighty. “The everlasting Father,” It says the everlasting Father because the one we thought was the heavenly Father, from the beginning, was always Christ. “The Prince of Peace.”

“Of the increase of his government” What is that word? Government. Some of you in here right now think the Lord is setting up a Sunday school church. No: he is setting up a government. The reason we always think Sunday school church is because black and brown people have never been a part of anything great, any kind of structural thing, so we always think low level. In every government there is a top guy: that is the Lord, he is going to be the top, and under him there is going to be the 12, then the rest of the 144 under that. There is going to be a government, a structural system set up. Right now this is proving ground: we are proving ourselves to the Lord, and he is going to choose who is worthy to sit in what seat.
